newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures rebound to finish higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures rebound to finish higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished higher, as buyers ignored concerns about higher U.S. interest rates and stepped into the market after two days of declines, traders and analysts said.
"Hedge funds were using end-of-month buying to come in as buyers on the first day of the month," one floor analyst said.
He said one hedge fund bought 3,000 September Standard & Poor 500s throughout the day through various houses, which helped turn the contract higher.
Overall, the U.S. equities markets rebounded due to extremely oversold conditions.
Similarly, the U.S. bond market attracted short-covering in a "dead-cat bounce" after conditions became oversold late last week, traders said.
Besides technical factors, fundamental factors also helped erase the bearish mood that lingered in both bond and stock markets from Friday.
The U.S. August National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index rose to 52.6, versus the average trade estimate of 52.9 and against July's 50.2.
"It's unrealistic to expect NAPM to stay near 50," said Kenneth Mayland, senior vice president of KeyCorp.
While the index and its individual components were higher, there were no indications of an "overheating economy," he said.
"In subsequent months, I would expect it to firm up and that would be consistent with a measured expansion of the economy," he said.

Nikkei futures also turned higher, with December closing near its daily high of 20,280.0. Spread trading continued, as traders rolled positions from September into December. December Nikkeis become lead contract month on September 12.
There were also signs of traders rolling positions into December, as the calendar spreads widened out, they said.
One hedge fund bought 900 contracts, which pushed the spread to six points, a trader said.
"That really caught a lot of people off guard," he said.
Fair value was at 0.78 to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 1.95 points to cash and arbitrage sell programs at a discount of 0.38 to cash.
In the final minutes of trade, one large U.S. firm bought S&Ps in 50 lot tranches for a total of 150 contracts, traders said.

At the end of pit trade, September S&Ps were up 4.50 at 655.85, NYSE new composite rose 1.45 at 352.40, KCBT Value Lines were up 0.60 at 617.30, Nikkeis up 45 at 20,230, Midcaps fell 1.10 to 231.35 and Nasdaqs were up 4.20 at 669.60. Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
